'''Daijingu''' (大神宮) is a name for shrines which are franches of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}. While the name implies a higher Rank than {{ill|List of Jingū|en|List of Jingū|qid=Q120680118|lt=Jingu}}, they are named in reference to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] and are different from the independently highly Ranked {{ill|List of Jingū|en|List of Jingū|qid=Q120680118|lt=Jingu}} Shrines on that article.
== List of Daijingu Shrines by Founding Year ==
* {{ill|Ōhi Shrine|en|Ōhi Shrine|qid=Q3090870|lt='''Funabashi Daijingū'''}}
* {{ill|Ino Tenshō Kōtai Jingū|ja伊勢山皇大神宮|2=ja|3=天照皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensho Kotaijingu|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshō Kōtai Jingū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17218394}} (天照皇大神宮)
** Location: {{ill|Kasuyagun Hisayamamachi|ja|糟屋郡久山町}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, Ino 604
** Nicknamed "Kyushu's Ise Shrine."
** Tradition holds that it was enshrined by {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, the consort of the 14th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Chūai}} and mother of the 15th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Ōjin}}.
** Moved to its current location around 1677 by {{ill|Kuroda Mitsuyuki|ja|黒田光之|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Mitsuyuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11678571}}.
* {{ill|Himukai-daijingū|ja|日向大神宮}} (日向大神宮)
** Nicknamed "Kyoto's Ise Shrine."
** Tradition states it was established by imperial decree of the 23rd Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|en|Emperor Kenzō|qid=Q360966|lt=Kenzo}}, enshrining the deity from the sacred site of Takachiho in Hyūga (modern-day {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|qid=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture}}).
* {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}
** The Inner Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}.
** The system of {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|式年遷宮|lt=Shikinen Sengū}} was established in the 14th year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|2=ja|3=天武天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q335181}} (685), with the first ceremony held in the 4th year of Emperor {{ill|Empress Jitō|en|Empress Jitō|qid=Q232026|lt=Jitō}} (690).
* {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮}}
** The Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}.
** The first {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|式年遷宮|lt=Shikinen Sengū}} was held in the 6th year of Emperor Jitō (692).
* {{ill|Yamaguchi Daijingu|ja|山口大神宮}}
** Nicknamed "The Ise Shrine of the West."
** Founded in 1520 (Eishō 17) by {{ill|Ōuchi Yoshioki|en|Ōuchi Yoshioki|qid=Q909270|lt=Ōuchi Yoshioki}}, the 30th head of the Ōuchi clan, who enshrined the deity of Ise Grand Shrine.
* {{ill|Isehara Daijingu|ja|伊勢原大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isehara Daijingu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11378955}}
** Nicknamed "The Ise Shrine of Kanto."
** Enshrined around 1620 by Yamada Soemon and others. There is no record of an imperial decree from {{ill|Emperor Go-Mizunoo|en|Emperor Go-Mizunoo|qid=Q320229|lt=Emperor Gomizunoo}}.
* {{ill|Kaiseizan Daijingū|ja|開成山大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaiseizan Daijingu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11655234}}
** Nicknamed "The Ise Shrine of Tohoku."
** Authorized by the Shrine Bureau in 1876 through the efforts of Chūjō Masatsune.
* {{ill|Tokyo Daijingu|en|Tokyo Daijingu|qid=Q11524717|lt=Tokyo Daijingu}}
** Nicknamed "The Ise Shrine of Tokyo."
** Established in 1880 as a remote worship hall of the Inner Shrine of Ise. Burned down in the 1923 {{ill|aftermath of 1923 Great Kantō earthquake|ja|関東大震災|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kanto Earthquake|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3742341}} and relocated to {{ill|Iidabashi|en|Iidabashi|qid=Q5994914|lt=Iidabashi}} in 1928.
* [[Ubagami Daijingū]]
** Located in Esahi Hokkaido
* {{ill|Iseyama Kōtai Jingu|ja伊勢山皇大神宮|Iseyama Kōtai Jingu}}
** Location: 64 Miyazaki-chō, Nishi-ku, Yokohama, Kanagawa Prefecture
** Nicknamed "The Ise Shrine of Kanto."
** Relocated to its current site in April 1870. Designated the principal shrine of Kanagawa Prefecture by the Meiji government in December 1870.
* Tensho Kotaijingu (てんしょうこうたいじんぐう)
** Location: Ida Nakanomachi, Nakahara-ku, Kawasaki City, Kanagawa Prefecture
* Tensho Kotaijingu (てんしょうこうたいじんぐう)
** Location: Oaza Kurakake, Azakamiwara, Tōmi City, Nagano Prefecture
